title: The identification: a round's junctions are the clusters of the unrolled candidate map
claim: Under RING-PAIR's scope (S1)-(S4) and (S5) the knot graph has a cycle: for every t >= 0 the junctions born in round t of the cheapest parity growth are in bijection with the deck orbits of clusters of t + 1 points of the universal cover of the candidate complex that contain a knot; parents are the removable points (pairwise distinct) and loose distinctions the boundary points (Theorem). Lemma 1: the incidence girth is at least 8; Lemma 2: a cluster and a nontrivial translate fit only in a cluster at least 4 points larger; Lemma 4: the groups are exactly the removable-point sets of the next clusters. Proposition 5: (S5) cannot be dropped (two stars joined at their centres, in RING-PAIR's scope, grows 6, 6, 2, 2, 4, 6, ... against the model's 6, 6, 2, 0).
standard_statement: Site animals on tree-like covers (Bethe lattices, Husimi trees: Fisher-Essam 1961; Harary-Uhlenbeck 1953); hyperbolic tree automorphisms (Serre 1980); block graphs (Harary 1963); reverse search over connected induced subgraphs (Avis-Fukuda 1996); halved graphs.
prior_work: RING-PAIR-20261119-001 (the model H, computed), CLUSTER-ALL-20261119-001 (the wider rule with chains and relays), FRESH-COUNT-20261118-001 (the policy).
